title: EventEnvelope
description: Fields carried by every Overpass event. These are not composed into event schemas via allOf: each event schema lists them explicitly and $refs the field definitions here. That is more verbose but keeps every event file readable on its own and keeps the Go and Python generators on their well-trodden paths. See contracts/README.md.

EventId.description: Unique identifier for this event instance. This is the deduplication key: consumers insert it into processed_events in the same transaction as the state change, so a redelivery hits the unique constraint and rolls back harmlessly. A retried publish of the same logical event MUST reuse the same event_id.

CorrelationId.description: Identifies the whole business transaction. Set once at ingress and propagated unchanged through every downstream event, so a single tasking request's entire fan-out is greppable in logs by one value.

CausationId.description: The event_id of the event that directly caused this one. Null only for events with no antecedent (ingress). Correlation gives you the tree; causation gives you the edges.

OccurredAt.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of when the fact became true in the producing service, NOT when it was published. Handlers use this plus state-machine guards to tolerate out-of-order arrival, because global ordering is explicitly not assumed.

SchemaVersion.description: Semantic version of this event's schema within the v1 major line. Adding an optional field is a minor bump. Removing a field, making an optional field required, or narrowing a type requires a new major line (a .v2 subject and a new schema file) — published schemas are never edited in place.

EventType.description: Fully qualified event type, identical to the NATS subject it is published on. Consumers dispatch on this rather than on subject, so replay from a file behaves identically to replay from the stream.

Producer.description: Service that emitted this event. Present for operability, not for routing — nothing may branch on producer, or the contract stops being a contract.
